body.p: The first non-final Office action on the merits dated August 6, 2024, and the references cited therein have been received and carefully reviewed. Favorable reconsideration of this application in view of the following remarks and discussion is respectfully requested.
Claims 1, 6, 11, and 15-18 are amended.
Claims 1-18 are currently pending for further examination and consideration.

p.u: Statement of the Substance of the Interview:

body.p: The Office action, the rejections raised therein, and some proposed amendments

reflected in the above amended claimset were discussed during a telephonic interview among the Applicant's representative, Amir Behnia (Reg. No. 50,215), Examiner Miller, andSupervisory Patent Examiner (SPE) Gort on November 4, 2024, for which, the Applicant and the Applicant's representative would like to thank Examiner Miller and SPE Gort for granting the interview and for their helpful comments and suggestions during the interview. Concerning the Applicant's Statement of the Substance of the Interview, Applicant respectfully states that the Applicant-Initiated Interview Summary (PTOL-413) correctly identifies all the participants, the date of the interview, the issues that were discussed, and correctly provides a detailed description of the substance of the interview.
As a result of the Office action, the drawings are objected to as failing to comply with 37 CFR 1.84(p)(5), as set forth on pages 2-3 of the Office action.
The specification and the claims are objected to because of informalities, as set forth on pages 3-4 of the Office action.
Claims 1, 6, 15, 17, and 18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being indefinite, as set forth on pages 3-10 of the Office action.
Claims 1-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 as being directed towards an abstract idea without significantly more, as set forth on pages 10-17 of the Office action.
The following obviousness rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 are raised against the
pending claims, as set forth on pages 18-39 of the Office action:

These rejections are respectfully traversed in view of the foregoing amendments and for at least the following reasons, and favorable reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims are therefore respectfully requested.
First, the drawings objections are respectfully traversed. Submitted herewith for approval by Examiner Miller are the attached Replacement Sheets of drawings including

changes to Figs. 2, 3, and 8. The Replacements Sheets replace original sheets 2, 3, and 9. No new matter is believed to have been added. As discussed and agreed during the interview, the amended drawing Figures overcome the objections and, hence, the objections are respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

The specification objections are respectfully traversed. As also discussed and agreed during the interview, by the above amendments to the specification, all of the informalities objections have been addressed, and are respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

The Section 112(b) rejections of claims 1, 6, 15, 17, and 18 are respectfully traversed. As also discussed and agreed during the interview, by the above amendments, Applicant believes all of the indefiniteness rejections have been addressed and, therefore, the indefiniteness rejections are respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

The Section 101 rejections of claims 1-18 are respectfully traversed. By the above amendments, claim 1 is amended to recite, among other features, "using the determined steering angle of the landing gear assembly to extend or retract the landing gear assembly". It was agreed that such amendment would make claim 1 patent eligible and, hence, it is respectfully requested that the Section 101 rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn.
Moreover, it was also agreed that claim 16 should not have been rejected under Section 101 and, hence, the Section 101 rejection of claim 16 will be withdrawn.

Also, concerning to claim 18, by the above amendments, the claim has been amended similarly to claim 1, however, it recites "using the determined steering angle of the landing gear assembly to steer the aircraft" rather than extending and retracting the landing. Applicant respectfully submits that such recitation would still overcome the Section 101
rejection and, therefore, it is respectfully requested that the Section 101 rejection of claim 18
be withdrawn.
The Section 103 obviousness rejection of claim 1 is respectfully traversed. Amended claim 1 now calls for:

determining the steering angle of the landing gear assembly from thefrom a shape and/or orientation of the identified boundary, and using the determined steering angle of the landing gear assembly to extend or retract the landing gear assembly.

Again, the Applicant and the Applicant's representative are appreciative of Examiner Miller and SPE Gort's helpful guidance during the interview. As Applicant's representative understood, it was tentatively agreed that if claim 1 is amended to recite: (1) the lidar system's location inside the landing gear bay, (2) explicit scanning of the torque link, and (3) extending and retracting the landing gear assembly using the determined steering angle, would overcome the current obviousness rejection by the combination of Kretschmann and He. Therefore, as amended claim 1 now requires: 1) a lidar system is mounted inside a landing gear space above the one or more wheels of the landing gear assembly, wherein the landing gear assembly comprises a torque link, 2) scanning the torque link of the landing gear assembly with the lidar system, and 3) extending and retracting the landing gear assembly using the determined steering angle, Applicant respectfully submits that amended claim 1 is patentable over the prior art combination, and the obviousness rejection of claim 1 is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.
The obviousness rejection of independent claim 16 is respectfully traversed. Claim

16 has been amended in a similar manner as claim 1 requiring the location of the lidar system mounted inside a landing gear space above the one or more wheels of the landing gear assembly, and scanning the torque link of the landing gear assembly with the lidar system. Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that amended claim 16 is patentable over the prior art combination, and the Section 103 rejection of claim 16 is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.
The obviousness rejection of independent claim 18 is respectfully traversed. Claim

18 has been amended in a similar manner as claim 1 requiring the location of the lidar system mounted inside a landing gear space above the one or more wheels of the landing gear assembly, however, claim 18 instead requires scanning the landing gear assembly with the lidar system to generate the set of three-dimensional position data points scanning the torque

link of the landing gear assembly with the lidar system. Applicant respectfully submits that amended claim 18 is still patentable over the prior art combination, and the Section 103 rejection of claim 18 is respectfully requested to be withdrawn.

Claims 2-15 depend from claim 1, recite additional features and distinguish over the applied references for at least the reasons set forth above with respect to claim 1 and/or for the additional features recited.

Claim 17 depends from claim 16, recites additional features and distinguishes over the applied references for at least the reasons set forth above with respect to claim 16 and/or for the additional features recited.
The Applicant has made a diligent effort to place the claims in condition for
allowance, and respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance, and an early notice to that effect is earnestly solicited.
